title: Complete current-group configuration transfer between devices

expectation.example: owner提供换季后的真实配置文件，AK151模板及当天航班均为21:05–23:05；目标设备仍有空时间AK151和文件之外的旧航班。owner确认新增换设备完整恢复选项，并暂不处理11月17日历史来源。
expectation.expected: 显式选择完整恢复后，共用模板和当前组当天航班逐项按文件恢复，文件之外旧航班不残留或被补回；开始结束时间和包含斜杠的完整岗位名称往返一致；生成及重排准备不再消费旧航班空时间。 Owner subsequently clarified that A-device export must carry all current-group long-term configuration and import seamlessly on B; complete imports must not mix in target-device old settings. Fix compound position names, zero fatigue and manual qualification roundtrip, and current-flight rename references. Follow-up: the same supplied config (15) must restore its existing valid flights and rules even when four newer statistics parameters and leave-type/half-rest tables are absent. Announce and apply central initial values only for those absent items; latest export must include them. Never silently inherit target-device values.
expectation.unchanged: Ordinary partial import is available after explicitly deselecting complete restore; history merge remains unchanged and the November 17 history investigation is deferred. Other-group existing staff, rule values, settings and current schedule remain unchanged; shared templates still add missing other-group rules. Admin support mode is intentionally excluded by the existing config contract. Scheduling eligibility, solver and fairness rules are unchanged. Owner subsequently explicitly chose to keep administrative support mode local to each device; imports preserve the target selection.
expectation.fallback: Full restore rejects required sections/parameters missing or any recorded invalid content before writing. The four newer morning/evening scalar values and absent leave/half-rest sections alone have an explicit, previewed initial-value recovery contract. Recorded invalid optional content, unresolved leave references and equal statistics interval endpoints (including after default compilation) remain rejected. Partial and history import contracts are unchanged.

answers.originalFailure: The original private file contains complete flight times, but normal config import preserves current flights and templates. Expanded red tests additionally expose slash splitting, zero-point fallback, manual-qualification loss, skipped rule tables and current-flight rename omissions. Evidence: config-transfer-red.txt, config-transfer-audit.json and final config-transfer-validation.txt. Follow-up evidence: owner confirmed the same config (15); overly strict missing-new-field checks blocked valid existing data. Two new red regressions also expose equal statistics intervals silently retaining device settings. An additional red failure was only a test-label typo and is not claimed as product evidence. Follow-up independent interface inventory guards against newly declared fields silently missing Excel; audit found no unexplained missing saved setting.
answers.laterChanges: Template auto-add can reintroduce old flights or source-deleted positions; complete restore now prevents both. Other-group nonempty schedules, initial preview versus confirmation, UI bypass, storage reload and second exports are explicitly tested. Current-flight rename reuses the existing current-group reference updater instead of duplicating a partial rule list. The single compileWorkbookConfigurationRestore handles defaults, validation, preview, option toggles and commit; UI integration verifies preview does not write, toggles remove/restore the notice and confirmation applies the announced values. Follow-up audit independently verifies each group through switch, persistence reload and second workbook transfer after editing, with the other group preserved (page-configuration-transfer-audit.json).
answers.finalArtifact: config-transfer-real.json independently checks 10 templates, 4 current flights and 82 rules from the supplied workbook and equal restored-business hashes across two differing target fixtures. Missing fields use defaults only in that diagnostic source fixture; this is not proof of the original A-device missing values. Actual A/B page acceptance remains unverified, and no deployment is claimed. config-optional-real.json now checks direct restoration of the supplied file on two different target stores, matching templates/flights/rules, removal of stale templates, storage reload and re-export with no missing optional values. Actual browser confirmation remains pending. Follow-up audit JSON and final verify log establish isolated complete transfers and 1737 functional / 19 performance passes, while physical-device comparison remains unverified.

review.missedScope: Initial flight-only repair missed rule position lists, manual qualifications, zero fatigue, source-deleted rules and default restoration mode. Expanded checks cover editors, XLSX, Store, UI, alternate imports and persistence. Real A-device unexported values, updated owner page and native WPS/Excel application opening remain unverified. Other-group whole-device backup and history replacement are outside the confirmed scope. Initial-value recovery does not recover A-device values absent from the original file. Actual browser/WPS/Excel and two physical devices remain unverified; no claim of final page acceptance. Follow-up audit distinguishes saved settings from unsaved drafts. Owner has explicitly confirmed keeping the verified administrative-mode exclusion; current-group export is not a full A/B backup.
review.rootCause: A partial merge workflow was treated as device restoration; current flights overrode replaced template times, missing fields reused local settings, and template synchronization could reconstruct deleted positions. Shared generic list parsing split compound names, manual markers replaced qualification IDs, and numeric falsy fallback changed zero. Current-flight rename maintained only a subset of existing rule references. The follow-up check incorrectly treated known missing newer fields as fatal. Settings normalization could also silently use a target-specific fallback for an equal start/end interval; complete restore now rejects that combination before writing. The follow-up inventory found no new unexplained omission; unsaved input uses the saved value by design and administrative mode is explicitly excluded by the current specification.
review.earlyDetection: Before a transfer change, use a source with changed flight names/times, slash positions, manual IDs, zero points, empty/deleted rule sets and nondefault settings. Export bytes and restore into two differently populated targets, compare all business fields and source rows independently, then reload/re-export and exercise the real confirmation path. Full files with missing/invalid configuration must not silently become successful partial restores. Include the actual previously exported file with absent newer fields, two target stores with different settings, and valid-versus-corrupt optional sections. Verify the announced defaults, direct confirmation, invalid interval rejection and a second full export. Independent TypeScript interface inventory now fails if a new ScheduleSettings or GroupWorkspace field lacks an explicit Excel or regenerated-state classification; use differing nondefault target settings and test save-before-export separately.
